PR #36 — baseline 6.0/10

what's good
  • Correct scope: it identifies and gates every real funnel a "plan mode" needs — runtime/tools/edits.py (writes), tools/shell.py (commands, with a READ_ONLY_PREFIXES allowlist so git status/ls still work), runtime/tools/approve.py (GH/HTTP mutations), runtime/mcp/manager.py (mutating MCP calls), and agents/orchestrator.py (spawn/settle refusal). Judge's PR only covers the last of these.
  • Genuinely good design details: tools/base.py's plan_mode_active(ctx) accepts either a bool or a zero-arg callable, and runtime/session.py threads a live lambda: self.plan_mode into child hooks — so a mid-session toggle is seen by already-running children without rebuilding their context. One shared PLAN_MODE_ERROR constant keeps the refusal message consistent everywhere.
  • Full protocol wiring: new SetPlanMode command, PlanModeChanged event, plan_mode field on the snapshot, and a working /plan on//plan off command in dummy_client.py — a real user-facing trigger exists, at least for one client.
  • The PR body is honest about its own gaps ("ran out of turns before completing (a), (c), full (d), and (e)").
issues
  • Verified regression, confirmed live on the PR's own CI run: tests/test_coverage_expansion.py::test_tool_run_command_with_config — a pre-existing, untouched test — now fails: AssertionError: assert 'exit code: 0' in 'error: plan mode is active...'. Root cause: the test builds ctx = Mock() without setting plan_mode; ToolContext.plan_mode defaults to False on the real dataclass, but a bare Mock() auto-generates a truthy, callable child attribute for anything it's asked for, so plan_mode_active(ctx) reads it as "plan mode is on." Reproduced independently (clone + pytest: 1 failed/1234 passed) and matches GitHub Actions run 35531640323, which is red right now.
  • Zero new tests for a safety-critical feature — the only automated coverage that touches plan mode at all is the one test it broke.
  • Self-admittedly incomplete per its own PR body, and one gap it doesn't mention: client_tui.py imports PlanModeChanged but never uses it (ruff --select F401 flags it) — the TUI client has no actual handling for the event, so plan-mode toggles are invisible there even though the wire protocol supports them.

PR #35 — judge 7.0/10

what's good
  • Everything it claims to do, it does, verified independently: cloned the branch, ran the full suite fresh — 1251 passed, 0 failed. The PR's own "62 total tests, all passing" claim checks out exactly (test_orchestrator_coverage.py + test_orchestrator.py = 62).
  • 17 new tests are genuinely well-targeted, not padding: case-insensitive approval ("yes" vs "Y"), the reject-then-revise loop, an exact allow-list check across all five spawnable profiles (coder/tester blocked, ask/researcher/debugger/reviewer allowed), and state transitions before/after approval.
  • Minimal, self-contained diff (2 files) with no ripple effects elsewhere in the codebase — nothing else to break.
  • Adds a novel mechanism baseline doesn't have: present_plan round-trips the plan text through child_ask_user for actual human approval/rejection with feedback, not just a blind toggle.
issues
  • Materially narrower than the feature implies: the only gate added is inside Orchestrator.spawn(), and only for profiles where needs_worktree is true. It does not touch runtime/tools/edits.py, tools/shell.py, runtime/tools/approve.py, or runtime/mcp/manager.py — so a coder agent already running when plan mode is entered can keep writing files, running shell commands, and opening PRs without any restriction. "Plan mode" here means "don't spawn a new writer," not "nothing risky happens."
  • No protocol-level wiring at all — no SetPlanMode command, no PlanModeChanged event, nothing in protocol/ or either client. The only way to enter plan mode is the orchestrator's own LLM deciding to call its new enter_plan_mode tool; a human user has no way to force it on from the TUI or CLI.
  • No handling for a rejected-then-abandoned plan other than "call present_plan again" — there's no way to exit plan mode without either an approval or the orchestrator giving up on its own.
verdict

Judge's PR is the one that's actually safe to merge today: everything in it is tested, its own claims check out exactly, and CI is green. But it's a much thinner slice of "plan mode" than the name promises — it only stops new writer spawns and has no human-facing trigger, so nothing in it would stop an in-flight coder from making changes once plan mode is on, or let a user turn it on from the TUI. Baseline scoped the problem correctly — it's the only one of the two that actually gates writes, shell, GH mutations, and MCP calls, with genuinely thoughtful cross-cutting design (the live-closure trick, the shared error constant) — but it shipped broken: a real, CI-confirmed regression in a pre-existing test, zero coverage of its own new code, and a dead import in the one client it didn't finish wiring. If forced to ship one today, judge's narrower-but-correct slice is the safer merge; baseline is the right design with none of the verification to back it up.

## Report

what: Surveyed the orchestrator/agent-harness codebase to scope adding a Claude-Code-style "Plan Mode" (investigate-only, no edits/mutating commands, plan text for user approval before real work).

paths (all facts also stored via remember, section=other):
- agents/orchestrator.py — Orchestrator(AgentLoop), the user-facing top-level agent. ORCH_SYSTEM prompt at top of file. Has no filesystem/write tools itself; spawns personalities as tools (spawn() at line 455) and owns settle_worktree (line 825).
- agents/agent_loop.py — AgentLoop, the shared tool-calling loop (run, _dispatch line 674, _execute_call line 720) used by both Orchestrator and Subagent. Central single dispatch: self._tools.execute(...).
- agents/subagent.py — Subagent(AgentLoop), what a spawned personality actually runs as; wires write_globs from the profile onto ToolContext.
- agents/profile.py — AgentProfile dataclass (tool_names, write_globs, required_tools, needs_worktree, etc.), ProfileRegistry, discover_profiles() (auto-discovery, no manual registry), tool-name bundles (NAV, EDIT, SHELL, GIT, GH_WRITE, etc).
- agents/profiles/{ask,coder,tester,researcher,debugger,reviewer}.py — one PROFILE = AgentProfile(...) per personality; read-only ones set write_globs=[] and omit EDIT/SHELL tool names; coder has write_globs=None (unrestricted); tester restricts to TEST_GLOBS.
- tools/base.py — Tool, ToolContext (carries write_globs, config, ask_user, etc.), @tool decorator.
- tools/registry.py — ToolRegistry (central registry: register, subset(names, profile), execute, schemas), discover_tools() auto-discovery.
- runtime/tools/edits.py — write funnel; _profile_write_error()/apply_edit() hard-enforce ctx.write_globs via runtime/tools/writeglob.py:write_allowed(). This is the real enforcement point (system prompt is not trusted).
- runtime/tools/approve.py, runtime/tools/shell.py, runtime/mcp/manager.py:_approve — existing per-call approval gating keyed on EngineConfig.exec_approval (auto/always/never), via ctx.ask_user(..., kind="confirm").
- runtime/config.py — EngineConfig dataclass + from_env(), loaded once in EngineSession.__init__; no existing "mode" concept.
- runtime/session.py — EngineSession, owns _config, builds Orchestrator in _bind_loop(), start_turn/_run_turn turn lifecycle.
- runtime/prompts.py — PromptBroker.ask() / UserPromptRequested event / AnswerPrompt command — the approve/confirm mechanism to reuse for "approve this plan?".
- protocol/commands.py, runtime/commands/register.py, runtime/commands/*.py, runtime/commands/__init__.py — command declare/dispatch pattern (@command, @handles), documented in docs/adding-a-command.md.
- app.py, dummy_client.py (slash-command parsing command_from_line), client_tui.py (Textual TUI, delegates to dummy_client), headless_client.py — CLI/UI entry points where a plan-mode toggle/command would surface.
- docs/adding-a-profile.md, docs/adding-a-command.md, docs/adding-a-tool.md, docs/impl-plans/orch-subagent-model.md — design docs describing these exact extension points.

verdict: No existing "mode"/read-only-mode/plan concept exists. Read-only enforcement today is per-profile (tool allowlist + write_globs glob gate in the write funnel) and per-call approval (exec_approval) — both fixed at session-start / profile-definition time, not a live toggle. Implementing Plan Mode is a net-new cross-cutting flag needing: (1) a live mutable flag reachable from EngineSession/Orchestrator (not just an env-loaded EngineConfig field, since it must toggle mid-session); (2) enforcement mirroring write_globs in runtime/tools/edits.py plus hard-denying run_command/mutating http_request/gh_*write/mutating MCP calls when active; (3) gating which profiles the orchestrator may spawn (exclude coder/tester/settle_worktree) and/or stripping EDIT/SHELL/GH_WRITE tool names from every spawned child while active; (4) a new protocol/commands.py command (e.g. SetPlanMode) + handler + optional event, wired through runtime/commands/__init__.py; (5) a client-side toggle in dummy_client.py/client_tui.py; (6) reuse of PromptBroker.ask(kind="confirm") for the "approve plan, exit plan mode" gate.

leftover: None outstanding — architecture is fully mapped for a coder to design the actual EngineConfig/session field, new command, and tool-gating changes. Did not check runtime/mcp/config.py/tokens.py internals or protocol/snapshot.py field-by-field, but those are peripheral to plan mode and only need touching if the UI needs to display plan-mode state in the snapshot.

paths touched
  • agents/orchestrator.py (Orchestrator, ORCH_SYSTEM prompt, spawn(), settle_worktree)
  • agents/agent_loop.py (AgentLoop shared loop: run/_dispatch/_execute_call, single dispatch via self._tools.execute)
leftover

runtime/mcp/config.py, runtime/mcp/tokens.py, and protocol/snapshot.py were not inspected field-by-field; only relevant if plan-mode state needs to appear in session snapshots sent to clients.

28|        out = ToolRegistry()

71|def discover_tools() -> ToolRegistry:

73|    registry = ToolRegistry()

  1|# Adding a subagent profile
  2|
  3|Profiles are discovered the same way tools are: drop a module under
  4|`agents/profiles/`, export `PROFILE = AgentProfile(...)`, and the orchestrator
  5|picks it up on the next `StartSession`. There is no registry file to edit.
  6|
  7|The orchestrator sees each profile as a **tool named after the profile**. Calling
  8|`ask` / `coder` / `tester` / … starts that child and returns immediately with
  9|`agent_id` (and `worktree` / `branch` when the profile writes). The child runs in
 10|the background. Tokens stream to the client tagged with `agent_id`. When it finishes, its transcript is compacted into an
 11|`AgentResult` string and delivered to the orch as a follow-up message (not as
 12|the original tool result). The child never chats with the user.
 13|
 14|## Who reads vs who writes
 15|
 16|The orchestrator is the planner, not a third reader. Typical edit:
 17|
 18|1. Spawn **ask** with the survey question. Stop. Do not also spawn coder in that turn.
 19|2. When ask's report arrives, spawn **coder** with paths, facts, and the change copied into the task.
 20|3. Coder `read_file`s those named paths (required before an edit) and writes. It should not `find` / search the tree unless a named path is missing.
 21|
 22|Skip a separate planner personality — that is the orch. Independent work (coder on a feature and debugger on an escalation) still runs in the same turn.
 23|
 24|## Minimal example
 25|
 26|```python
 27|# agents/profiles/docs.py
 28|from agents.profile import NAV, AgentProfile
 29|
 30|PROFILE = AgentProfile(
 31|    name="docs",
 32|    description="Write or update markdown docs. Cannot edit application code.",
 33|    system_prompt="You only touch documentation files. ...",
 34|    tool_names=NAV + ["str_replace", "create_file", "read_file"],
 35|    write_globs=["**/*.md", "**/docs/**"],
 36|    required_tools=[],
 37|    max_turns=8,
 38|    needs_worktree=False,
 39|)
 40|```
 41|
 42|Restart the session (or call `discover_profiles()` in a test). The orch model
 43|will see a `docs` tool with a `task` argument.
 44|
 45|## Examples
 46|
 47|Three end-to-end recipes, from simplest to most involved.
 48|
 49|### Example A: a profile with no tools at all
 50|
 51|Some personalities only need to reason over the task text and conversation
 52|history — no filesystem, no shell, nothing. Set `tool_names=[]` and
 53|`write_globs=[]` so it is a hard no-op even if a future edit to the profile
 54|accidentally adds a tool name.
 55|
 56|```python
 57|# agents/profiles/planner.py
 58|from __future__ import annotations
 59|from agents.profile import AgentProfile
 60|
 61|PLANNER_SYSTEM = """You are a planning-only agent. You do not read files,
 62|run commands, or edit anything. Given a task description and any facts
 63|already provided in the prompt, produce a short ordered plan (steps, owners,
 64|risks). If you need information you were not given, say so explicitly and
 65|stop — do not guess at file paths or code contents."""
 66|
 67|PROFILE = AgentProfile(
 68|    name="planner",
 69|    description=(
 70|        "Turns a fuzzy task into an ordered plan using only the text it was "
 71|        "given. Has no tools — cannot read the repo or verify anything. Use "
 72|        "only when the caller already has the facts and just wants them "
 73|        "organized."
 74|    ),
 75|    system_prompt=PLANNER_SYSTEM,
 76|    tool_names=[],
 77|    write_globs=[],
 78|    required_tools=[],
 79|    max_turns=4,
 80|    needs_worktree=False,
 81|)
 82|```
 83|
 84|Nothing else to wire up — dropping this file under `agents/profiles/` is the
 85|entire registration step. Restart the session (or call `discover_profiles()`
 86|in a test) and the orch model will see a `planner(task=...)` tool.
 87|
 88|### Example B: a profile reusing existing tools
 89|
 90|Most new personalities just need a different combination of to

  1|# Adding a new command
  2|
  3|Commands are the client → server half of the engine's Unix-socket protocol
  4|(NDJSON over `.engine/engine.sock`); events are the server → client half. This
  5|doc covers adding a **command**. If you also need a new outbound message, see
  6|the analogous `@event` pattern in `protocol/events.py` (same idea, registered
  7|in `EVENTS` instead of `COMMANDS`).
  8|
  9|Like tools, commands are declared once and picked up by decorator-based
 10|registries — no central dispatch `if/elif` chain to extend.
 11|
 12|## The pieces
 13|
 14|- `protocol/message.py` — `ProtocolMessage`, the base dataclass every command
 15|  and event inherits. Gives you `to_json()`/`from_json()` for free based on
 16|  dataclass fields and type hints (including `Optional[X]` and `list[X]` of
 17|  another `ProtocolMessage`).
 18|- `protocol/commands.py` — one `@command @dataclass` class per command. The
 19|  `@command` decorator registers the class in `COMMANDS: dict[str, type]` by
 20|  class name, which `decode_command` uses to route an incoming `{"type": ...}`
 21|  JSON object back to the right dataclass.
 22|- `protocol/codec.py` — `encode`/`decode_command`/`decode_event`. NDJSON: one
 23|  JSON object per line, always with a `"type"` field.
 24|- `runtime/commands/register.py` — `HANDLERS: dict[type, callable]` and the
 25|  `@handles(CommandType)` decorator that fills it.
 26|- `runtime/commands/*.py` — handler implementations, grouped by area
 27|  (`lifecycle.py`, `files.py`, `git.py`, `agent.py`). Add a new function to an
 28|  existing module if your command fits, or add a new module.
 29|- `runtime/commands/__init__.py` — imports every handler module for its side
 30|  effects (so the `@handles` decorators run and populate `HANDLERS`). **You
 31|  must add your new module here if you create one** — this is the one place
 32|  that isn't fully automatic (unlike `tools/`, which walks the package
 33|  directory itself).
 34|- `runtime/session.py` — `EngineSession.handle(command)` looks up
 35|  `HANDLERS[type(command)]` and calls it (awaiting if async). This is also
 36|  where most of the state your handler will touch lives (`_state`, `_workspace`,
 37|  `_emit`, `_persist`, ...).
 38|
 39|## Minimal example
 40|
 41|```python
 42|# protocol/commands.py
 43|@command
 44|@dataclass
 45|class RenameSession(ProtocolMessage):
 46|    name: str
 47|```
 48|
 49|```python
 50|# runtime/commands/lifecycle.py (or a new module)
 51|from protocol.commands import RenameSession
 52|from protocol.events import ErrorOccurred
 53|from runtime.commands.register import handles
 54|
 55|
 56|@handles(RenameSession)
 57|def rename_session(session, command: RenameSession) -> None:
 58|    if not session._require_session():
 59|        return
 60|    if not command.name.strip():
 61|        session._emit(ErrorOccurred(message="name must not be empty"))
 62|        return
 63|    session._state.name = command.name.strip()
 64|    session._persist()
 65|```
 66|
 67|If it's a new module, add it to `runtime/commands/__init__.py`:
 68|
 69|```python
 70|from runtime.commands import lifecycle as _lifecycle  # noqa: F401
 71|from runtime.commands import my_module as _my_module  # noqa: F401  # add this
 72|```
 73|
 74|That's the whole integration — the codec already knows how to decode
 75|`RenameSession` (dataclass fields + `@command`), and `EngineSession.handle`
 76|already knows how to route it to `rename_session` (via `HANDLERS`).
 77|
 78|## Defining the command dataclass
 79|
 80|- Inherit `ProtocolMessage`, decorate with `@command` **then** `@dataclass`
 81|  (order matters: `@command` reads `cls.__name__` after the dataclass is
 82|  built, so `@dataclass` must be the inner decorator, applied first).
 83|- Field types matter — `from_json`/`to_json` use them:
 84|  - Plain `str`/`int`/`float`/`bool`/`list[str]` round-trip as-is.
 85|  - `X | None` fields are om

 740|upserts. Only durable state is persisted — the file tree, git state, and
 741|detected language are stripped before writing, since all three are recomputed
 742|from disk on load. Sessions are listed newest-saved-first.
 743|
 744|State is persisted after every user message, agent reply, file open, file
 745|close, and on shutdown. File notes and decisions are written when an agent
 746|calls `remember`, and when ask / coder / researcher finish (the labeled
 747|briefing is ingested with no extra model call). `touch` on `read_file` and
 748|successful edits only refreshes `seen_sha` for files that already have a
 749|note; empty touches are not stored. A file note is marked `STALE` when the
 750|current disk hash does not match the hash stored with the note.

 754|## Configuration
 755|
 756|| Variable | Default | Purpose |
 757||---|---|---|
 758|| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | — | Required for chat. Placeholder values (`...`, `your-key`, `changeme`, `<OPENROUTER_API_KEY>`) are treated as unset. |
 759|| `OPENROUTER_MODEL` | `openai/gpt-4o-mini` | Any OpenRouter model with tool-calling support. |
 760|| `OPENROUTER_CHILD_MODEL` | (unset) | Fallback model for profiles that do not set `AgentProfile.model`. |
 761|| `ENGINE_LLM_STREAM` | `1` | Set `0` to disable token streaming. |
 762|| `ENGINE_LLM_TIMEOUT_S` | `600` | LLM request timeout. |
 763|| `ENGINE_LLM_IDLE_S` | `90` | Stream idle timeout. |
 764|| `ENGINE_MAX_TURNS` | `16` | Tool-calling turns per user message. |
 765|| `ENGINE_MAX_SPAWNS_PER_TURN` | `8` | Live concurrent subagents (not reset each orch reply). |
 766|| `ENGINE_EXEC_APPROVAL` | `auto` | `auto`, `always`, or `never`. |
 767|| `ENGINE_EXEC_TIMEOUT_S` | `120` | Default `run_command` timeout. |
 768|| `ENGINE_EXEC_FILE_LIMIT_MB` | `2048` | `ulimit -f` cap (POSIX 512-byte blocks). |
 769|| `ENGINE_CONTEXT_BUDGET` | `120000` | Compaction trigger budget. |
 770|| `ENGINE_PUSHGATEWAY_URL` | (unset) | Prometheus Pushgateway base URL. Unset disables pushes; metrics still accumulate in-process. |
 771|| `ENGINE_METRICS_JOB` | `engine` | Pushgateway job name. Grouping key `instance` is the session id unless overridden. |
 772|| `ENGINE_METRICS_INSTANCE` | (session id) | Pushgateway grouping key `instance`. Set to a stable name (e.g. `baseline`) when comparing runs. |
 773|| `ENGINE_METRICS_PUSH_INTERVAL_S` | `2` | Debounce between pushes; turn end, agent finish, and session close always flush. |
 774|
 775|Set them in the environment or in `env.sh` at the workspace root. `env.sh`
 776|parsing is deliberately minimal — it handles `export`, `#` comments, and quoted

 25|
 26|# Orchestrator and subagent personalities
 27|
 28|The original class-design plan already specified this layer ([`.cursor/plans/engine_class_design_9b10c713.plan.md`](engine-class-design.md) step 5). The engine today still has one [`AgentLoop`](../../agents/agent_loop.py) bound in [`EngineSession._bind_loop`](../../runtime/session.py) with **all 24 tools**, and [`AbortAgent(agent_id=...)`](../../runtime/commands/agent.py) still returns `"subagents are not implemented"`. This slice implements that missing layer, with updated personalities and a tool-like extension model.
 29|
 30|## Design decisions
 31|
 32|**User talks only to the orchestrator.** `SubmitUserMessage` always runs the orch loop. Subagent tokens never become `ChatMessageAdded` / `ChatMessageDelta` in the user chat. Clients see subagents via `AgentStarted` / `AgentStateChanged(agent_id=...)` / `AgentFinished` plus tool events tagged with `agent_id`.
 33|
 34|**The orch does not do the work.** It never writes files and never runs shell. It may:
 35|
 36|- Answer directly when the reply is already in chat / `.engine/context.md`, or is a meta question (status, what just happened).
 37|- Use a **small read set** (`list_files`, `search`, `read_file`, `list_symbols`) only to write a better spawn prompt — not to investigate a whole question itself.
 38|- Spawn one or more personalities with a task string (“writer prompt”).
 39|- After compacted results return, synthesize the user-facing answer, or `request_user_input` / respawn.
 40|
 41|**Personalities are discovered like tools.** Drop a module under `agents/profiles/`, export a profile object. No registry file to edit. The orch sees each personality as a **callable tool named after the profile** (`ask`, `coder`, …), not one generic `spawn_agent` enum. That matches “agents designed like tools.”
 42|
 43|**Subagents compact, then return.** On finish (or abort / max-turns), the subagent transcript is summarized into a structured `AgentResult`. That string is the orch’s tool result. Full subagent history is dropped. A short note is appended to `.engine/context.md` (already injected into `_build_messages()` via [`read_context_md`](../../agents/compactor.py)).
 44|
 45|**One use

  • Live plan_mode flag on EngineSession
  • Threaded through ToolContext
  • Hard enforcement at the write funnel (runtime/tools/edits.py), run_command (runtime/tools/shell.py), and mutating GitHub/MCP calls — not just prompt text

  • New SetPlanMode command wired through the existing command-registration pattern, with client notification
  • ORCH_SYSTEM prompt updated to require investigate → present plan → ask for approval via the existing confirm mechanism → toggle off → proceed
  • /plan slash command in dummy_client.py and client_tui.py

  1|# Adding a new command
  2|
  3|Commands are the client → server half of the engine's Unix-socket protocol
  4|(NDJSON over `.engine/engine.sock`); events are the server → client half. This
  5|doc covers adding a **command**. If you also need a new outbound message, see
  6|the analogous `@event` pattern in `protocol/events.py` (same idea, registered
  7|in `EVENTS` instead of `COMMANDS`).
  8|
  9|Like tools, commands are declared once and picked up by decorator-based
 10|registries — no central dispatch `if/elif` chain to extend.
 11|
 12|## The pieces
 13|
 14|- `protocol/message.py` — `ProtocolMessage`, the base dataclass every command
 15|  and event inherits. Gives you `to_json()`/`from_json()` for free based on
 16|  dataclass fields and type hints (including `Optional[X]` and `list[X]` of
 17|  another `ProtocolMessage`).
 18|- `protocol/commands.py` — one `@command @dataclass` class per command. The
 19|  `@command` decorator registers the class in `COMMANDS: dict[str, type]` by
 20|  class name, which `decode_command` uses to route an incoming `{"type": ...}`
 21|  JSON object back to the right dataclass.
 22|- `protocol/codec.py` — `encode`/`decode_command`/`decode_event`. NDJSON: one
 23|  JSON object per line, always with a `"type"` field.
 24|- `runtime/commands/register.py` — `HANDLERS: dict[type, callable]` and the
 25|  `@handles(CommandType)` decorator that fills it.
 26|- `runtime/commands/*.py` — handler implementations, grouped by area
 27|  (`lifecycle.py`, `files.py`, `git.py`, `agent.py`). Add a new function to an
 28|  existing module if your command fits, or add a new module.
 29|- `runtime/commands/__init__.py` — imports every handler module for its side
 30|  effects (so the `@handles` decorators run and populate `HANDLERS`). **You
 31|  must add your new module here if you create one** — this is the one place
 32|  that isn't fully automatic (unlike `tools/`, which walks the package
 33|  directory itself).
 34|- `runtime/session.py` — `EngineSession.handle(command)` looks up
 35|  `HANDLERS[type(command)]` and calls it (awaiting if async). This is also
 36|  where most of the state your handler will touch lives (`_state`, `_workspace`,
 37|  `_emit`, `_persist`, ...).
 38|
 39|## Minimal example
 40|
 41|```python
 42|# protocol/commands.py
 43|@command
 44|@dataclass
 45|class RenameSession(ProtocolMessage):
 46|    name: str
 47|```
 48|
 49|```python
 50|# runtime/commands/lifecycle.py (or a new module)
 51|from protocol.commands import RenameSession
 52|from protocol.events import ErrorOccurred
 53|from runtime.commands.register import handles
 54|
 55|
 56|@handles(RenameSession)
 57|def rename_session(session, command: RenameSession) -> None:
 58|    if not session._require_session():
 59|        return
 60|    if not command.name.strip():
 61|        session._emit(ErrorOccurred(message="name must not be empty"))
 62|        return
 63|    session._state.name = command.name.strip()
 64|    session._persist()
 65|```
 66|
 67|If it's a new module, add it to `runtime/commands/__init__.py`:
 68|
 69|```python
 70|from runtime.commands import lifecycle as _lifecycle  # noqa: F401
 71|from runtime.commands import my_module as _my_module  # noqa: F401  # add this
 72|```
 73|
 74|That's the whole integration — the codec already knows how to decode
 75|`RenameSession` (dataclass fields + `@command`), and `EngineSession.handle`
 76|already knows how to route it to `rename_session` (via `HANDLERS`).
 77|
 78|## Defining the command dataclass
 79|
 80|- Inherit `ProtocolMessage`, decorate with `@command` **then** `@dataclass`
 81|  (order matters: `@command` reads `cls.__name__` after the dataclass is
 82|  built, so `@dataclass` must be the inner decorator, applied first).
 83|- Field types matter — `from_json`/`to_json` use them:
 84|  - Plain `str`/`int`/`float`/`bool`/`list[str]` round-trip as-is.
 85|  - `X | None` fields are om

809|def batch_nickname(task: str, *, limit: int = 48) -> str:
810|    text = (task or "").strip()

815|        text = f"after {profile}"
816|    else:
817|        text = " ".join(text.replace("\n", " ").split())
818|    if not text:
819|        return "untitled"
820|    if len(text) > limit:
821|        return text[: limit - 3] + "..."
822|    return text

 4|async def require_approval(ctx, question: str) -> str:
 5|    """Return an error string if the user denies, else empty.
 6|
 7|    `never` skips the prompt. `always`/`auto` ask when ask_user is set.
 8|    No ask_user: `always` denies, `auto` allows.
 9|    """
10|    approval = "auto"
11|    if ctx is not None and getattr(ctx, "config", None) is not None:
12|        approval = getattr(ctx.config, "exec_approval", "auto") or "auto"
13|    approval = str(approval).strip().lower()
14|    if approval == "never":
15|        return ""
16|    ask = getattr(ctx, "ask_user", None) if ctx is not None else None
17|    if ask is None:
18|        if approval == "always":
19|            return "error: user denied"
20|        return ""
21|    # Unknown values prompt (same as auto). Do not fail open.
22|    answer = await ask(question, kind="confirm")
23|    if str(answer).strip().lower() not in {"yes", "y"}:
24|        return "error: user denied"
25|    return ""

385|        advertised: set[str] = set()

387|            advertised |= state.advertised
388|        err = scheme_allowed(uri, advertised or None)
389|        if err:
390|            return err
391|        last = "error: no MCP server could read the resource"
392|        for state in self.servers.values():

 1|from __future__ import annotations
 2|
 3|import fnmatch
 4|
 5|
 6|def write_allowed(rel: str, globs: list[str] | None) -> bool:
 7|    """None = any path; empty list = none; otherwise match any glob."""
 8|    if globs is None:
 9|        return True
10|    if not globs:
11|        return False
12|    rel = rel.replace("\\", "/").lstrip("./")
13|    name = rel.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
14|    for pattern in globs:
15|        pat = pattern.replace("\\", "/")
16|        if fnmatch.fnmatch(rel, pat) or fnmatch.fnmatch(name, pat):
17|            return True
18|        if pat.startswith("**/") and pat.endswith("/**"):
19|            mid = pat[3:-3]
20|            if not mid:
21|                return True
22|            if rel == mid or rel.startswith(mid + "/") or f"/{mid}/" in f"/{rel}/":
23|                return True
24|    return False

186|    text = line.removeprefix("/")
187|    parts = text.split(maxsplit=1)
188|    name = parts[0].lower()
189|    rest = parts[1].strip() if len(parts) > 1 else ""

193|def command_from_line(line: str, workspace: Path):
194|    name, rest = _split(line)
195|    if name == "help":
196|        _note(_help_text().rstrip("\n"))
197|        return None
198|    if name in ("exit", "quit"):
199|        return CLIENT_EXIT
200|    if name in ("start", "startsession"):
201|        return StartSession(
202|            workspace=str(workspace),
203|            session_id=rest or None,
204|        )
205|    if name in ("undo", "undolastedit"):
206|        return UndoLastEdit()
207|    if name in ("snapshot", "snap", "requestsnapshot"):
208|        return RequestSnapshot(replay=False)
209|    if name in ("context", "orchcontext", "requestorchcontext"):
210|        return RequestOrchContext()
211|    if name in ("abort", "abortagent"):
212|        return AbortAgent(agent_id=rest or None)
213|    if name in ("answer", "answerprompt"):
214|        if not _LAST_PROMPT_ID:
215|            _note("no prompt is outstanding")
216|            return None
217|        if not rest:
218|            _note("usage: answer <text>  (or type the answer at the answer> prompt)")
219|            return None
220|        return _take_answer(rest)
221|    cls = _COMMANDS_BY_NAME.get(name)
222|    if cls is StartSession:
223|        return StartSession(
224|            workspace=str(workspace),
225|            session_id=rest or None,
226|        )
227|    if cls is SubmitUserMessage:
228|        if not rest:
229|            _note("usage: SubmitUserMessage <text>")
230|            return None
231|        return SubmitUserMessage(text=rest)
232|    if cls is not None:
233|        names = [item.name for item in fields(cls)]
234|        if not names:
235|            return cls()

 39|def escape(text: str) -> str:
 40|    # Library escape() only covers [tag]-like spans; JSON `[{...}]` still opens a tag.
 41|    text = text.replace("[", "\\[")
 42|    if text.endswith("\\") and not text.endswith("\\\\"):
 43|        return text + "\\"
 44|    return text

docs/adding-a-command.md  lines 1-200 of 249  (next offset=201)
  1|# Adding a new command
  2|
  3|Commands are the client → server half of the engine's Unix-socket protocol
  4|(NDJSON over `.engine/engine.sock`); events are the server → client half. This
  5|doc covers adding a **command**. If you also need a new outbound message, see
  6|the analogous `@event` pattern in `protocol/events.py` (same idea, registered
  7|in `EVENTS` instead of `COMMANDS`).
  8|
  9|Like tools, commands are declared once and picked up by decorator-based
 10|registries — no central dispatch `if/elif` chain to extend.
 11|
 12|## The pieces
 13|
 14|- `protocol/message.py` — `ProtocolMessage`, the base dataclass every command
 15|  and event inherits. Gives you `to_json()`/`from_json()` for free based on
 16|  dataclass fields and type hints (including `Optional[X]` and `list[X]` of
 17|  another `ProtocolMessage`).
 18|- `protocol/commands.py` — one `@command @dataclass` class per command. The
 19|  `@command` decorator registers the class in `COMMANDS: dict[str, type]` by
 20|  class name, which `decode_command` uses to route an incoming `{"type": ...}`
 21|  JSON object back to the right dataclass.
 22|- `protocol/codec.py` — `encode`/`decode_command`/`decode_event`. NDJSON: one
 23|  JSON object per line, always with a `"type"` field.
 24|- `runtime/commands/register.py` — `HANDLERS: dict[type, callable]` and the
 25|  `@handles(CommandType)` decorator that fills it.
 26|- `runtime/commands/*.py` — handler implementations, grouped by area
 27|  (`lifecycle.py`, `files.py`, `git.py`, `agent.py`). Add a new function to an
 28|  existing module if your command fits, or add a new module.
 29|- `runtime/commands/__init__.py` — imports every handler module for its side
 30|  effects (so the `@handles` decorators run and populate `HANDLERS`). **You
 31|  must add your new module here if you create one** — this is the one place
 32|  that isn't fully automatic (unlike `tools/`, which walks the package
 33|  directory itself).
 34|- `runtime/session.py` — `EngineSession.handle(command)` looks up
 35|  `HANDLERS[type(command)]` and calls it (awaiting if async). This is also
 36|  where most of the state your handler will touch lives (`_state`, `_workspace`,
 37|  `_emit`, `_persist`, ...).
 38|
 39|## Minimal example
 40|
 41|```python
 42|# protocol/commands.py
 43|@command
 44|@dataclass
 45|class RenameSession(ProtocolMessage):
 46|    name: str
 47|```
 48|
 49|```python
 50|# runtime/commands/lifecycle.py (or a new module)
 51|from protocol.commands import RenameSession
 52|from protocol.events import ErrorOccurred
 53|from runtime.commands.register import handles
 54|
 55|
 56|@handles(RenameSession)
 57|def rename_session(session, command: RenameSession) -> None:
 58|    if not session._require_session():
 59|        return
 60|    if not command.name.strip():
 61|        session._emit(ErrorOccurred(message="name must not be empty"))
 62|        return
 63|    session._state.name = command.name.strip()
 64|    session._persist()
 65|```
 66|
 67|If it's a new module, add it to `runtime/commands/__init__.py`:
 68|
 69|```python
 70|from runtime.commands import lifecycle as _lifecycle  # noqa: F401
 71|from runtime.commands import my_module as _my_module  # noqa: F401  # add this
 72|```
 73|
 74|That's the whole integration — the codec already knows how to decode
 75|`RenameSession` (dataclass fields + `@command`), and `EngineSession.handle`
 76|already knows how to route it to `rename_session` (via `HANDLERS`).
 77|
 78|## Defining the command dataclass
 79|
 80|- Inherit `ProtocolMessage`, decorate with `@command` **then** `@dataclass`
 81|  (order matters: `@command` reads `cls.__name__` after the dataclass is
 82|  built, so `@dataclass` must be the inner decorator, applied first).
 83|- Field types matter — `from_json`/`to_json` use them:
 84|  - Plain `str`/`int`/`float`/`bool`/`list[str]` round-trip as-is.
 85|  - `X | None` fields are om

 4|async def require_approval(ctx, question: str) -> str:
 5|    """Return an error string if the user denies, else empty.

warn reviewer aaa824c4 $0.566 · 958,058 tok

Investigation complete given remaining turn budget. Reporting final verdict.

Spec item 1 — live plan_mode flag threaded into ToolContext (runtime/session.py, agents/subagent.py, agents/agent_loop.py, agents/orchestrator.py): PARTIALLY DONE / BROKEN.
- EngineSession.plan_mode: bool = False exists (runtime/session.py:97) and is forwarded as plan_mode=lambda: self.plan_mode into Orchestrator(...) (runtime/session.py:394), which flows through AgentLoop.__init__'s new plan_mode param (agents/agent_loop.py:122,144-163) into the orchestrator's own ToolContext. That path is correct.
- tools/base.py adds ToolContext.plan_mode: Any = False and a plan_mode_active() helper (tools/base.py:31,38-44) that accepts bool or zero-arg callable. Correct design.
- Bug: Orchestrator._make_subagent (agents/orchestrator.py:762-821) builds every Subagent(...) (coder/tester/ask/researcher/debugger/reviewer) without passing plan_mode=. Subagent (agents/subagent.py) never sets a default either. So every child's own ToolContext.plan_mode falls back to AgentLoop.__init__'s default plan_mode=None (agent_loop.py:122), which plan_mode_active() evaluates as bool(None) == False — always. Net effect: none of the per-tool plan-mode checks in runtime/tools/edits.py, tools/shell.py, runtime/tools/approve.py, runtime/mcp/manager.py will ever fire inside a spawned child, because the child's ctx.plan_mode is permanently None/False regardless of EngineSession.plan_mode. This matters concretely for debugger, whose profile includes SHELL (agents/profiles/debugger.py:41) — a debugger's run_command is not actually blocked during plan mode despite the check in tools/shell.py:43, because ctx.plan_mode there is None. Coder/tester are blocked from ever spawning (item 3), so this only silently defeats the funnel for read-only-profile children (debugger's shell) — but that is exactly the gap the spec calls out as needing enforcement.

Spec item 2 — enforcement at funnel points: DONE at the code-shape level, contingent on item 1's bug.
- runtime/tools/edits.py:_profile_write_error (line 655) and undo_last_sync (line 869) both call plan_mode_active(ctx) and return PLAN_MODE_ERROR.
- tools/shell.py:run_command (lines 43-50) denies unless the stripped command matches READ_ONLY_PREFIXES (imported correctly from runtime/tools/shell.py:19).
- runtime/tools/approve.py:require_approval (line 16) denies before any approval logic — this correctly covers mutating gh_pr_comment/gh_issue_create/gh_pr_create (tools/github.py:339,360,388) and mutating http_request (tools/http.py:44, gated on SAFE_METHODS), so GET/HEAD stay unaffected. Good, minimal, correct routing.
- runtime/mcp/manager.py:_approve (line 434) checks plan_mode_active(ctx) before proceeding.
- All of this is correctly wired for the orchestrator's ctx, but per item 1's bug, plan_mode is never true in any child ctx, so this enforcement is effectively dead for spawned agents (debugger's shell in particular).

Spec item 3 — orchestrator refuses to spawn coder/tester and refuses settle_worktree in plan mode: DONE.
- agents/orchestrator.py:463-464 _in_plan_mode(), :471-477 in spawn() denies non-_PLAN_MODE_ALLOWED profiles ({"ask","researcher","debugger","reviewer"}, line 827) with the specified message.
- settle_worktree (line 339-347) checks _in_plan_mode() and returns the plan-mode error before proceeding, correctly placed after the status/list short-circuit.

Spec item 4 — SetPlanMode command: NOT DONE.
- protocol/commands.py has no SetPlanMode class; grep for SetPlanMode|PlanMode across runtime/commands/*, protocol/commands.py, dummy_client.py, client_tui.py, tests/ finds zero hits except comments in runtime/session.py and agents/orchestrator.py referencing it by name as documentation/aspiration. No handler registered in runtime/commands/register.py/__init__.py. EngineSession.plan_mode currently has no way to be set to True at all — it is write-once-false, dead code from the user's perspective. This is the single biggest missing piece; nothing in the feature is reachable end-to-end without it.

Spec item 5 — ORCH_SYSTEM prompt updated for plan mode / PromptBroker confirm before exiting: NOT DONE.
- agents/orchestrator.py:33-76 (ORCH_SYSTEM) has zero mention of plan mode, read-only-only investigation, or an approval gate to exit plan mode. No PromptBroker.ask(..., kind="confirm") call added anywhere for a plan-mode-exit flow (existing kind="confirm" usages are pre-existing exec-approval/MCP call sites, runtime/tools/approve.py:30, runtime/mcp/manager.py:452, unrelated to this feature).

Spec item 6 — /plan on//plan off in dummy_client.py, toggle in client_tui.py: NOT DONE.
- No matches for /plan, plan_mode, or SetPlanMode in either dummy_client.py or client_tui.py.

Spec item 7 — diagnostics clean on touched files: Mixed, but the plan-mode-relevant diagnostics are clean; pre-existing unrelated Pyright noise remains.
- Clean: agents/orchestrator.py, runtime/tools/edits.py, runtime/tools/approve.py.
- tools/base.py: 2 Pyright errors (fn._engine_tool assignment, inspect.get_type_hints) — both on lines outside the diff (decorator machinery at 109/117), pre-existing, not introduced by this change.
- runtime/session.py, agents/agent_loop.py, runtime/commands/lifecycle.py, runtime/commands/agent.py, tools/shell.py, runtime/mcp/manager.py: dozens of Pyright errors, but all are about ProtocolMessage/dataclass attribute access (e.g. No parameter named "message", Cannot access attribute "agent_id" for class "ProtocolMessage") and unrelated typing mismatches (approve callback signature in shell, MCP errlog/elicitation typing) — none reference plan_mode, and line numbers fall outside the diff hunks in every file I checked (e.g. tools/shell.py:72 in the unchanged run_command_impl call block; runtime/session.py errors are scattered across ~40 unrelated lines, none near line 97/394). These read as a pre-existing, repo-wide Pyright/stub mismatch (ProtocolMessage dataclass fields not recognized), not something this diff caused — but I could not fully diff against a clean baseline in the remaining budget, so flag for the next coder to double check with a quick git stash+diagnostics if in doubt.

verdict

request changes — the feature is not usable end-to-end. Item 4 (SetPlanMode command) is completely missing, item 6 (slash commands) is completely missing, item 5 (prompt/confirm flow) is completely missing, and item 1 has a real bug (child ToolContext never receives the live plan_mode signal). Items 2/3 are well-implemented and can stay as-is.

facts

(1) Orchestrator._make_subagent at agents/orchestrator.py:798-821 never passes plan_mode= into Subagent(...), so every child ToolContext's plan_mode is None regardless of EngineSession.plan_mode, defeating edits/shell/mcp enforcement inside any spawned agent (concretely debugger's run_command, since debugger has SHELL tools per agents/profiles/debugger.py:41). (2) No SetPlanMode command exists in protocol/commands.py (22 @command classes present, none named that) and no handler in runtime/commands/register.py or any runtime/commands/*.py file — EngineSession.plan_mode (runtime/session.py:97) can never be flipped to True by any client. (3) ORCH_SYSTEM (agents/orchestrator.py:33-76) has no plan-mode guidance and no PromptBroker.ask(kind="confirm") exit-approval flow. (4) No /plan slash command in dummy_client.py or client_tui.py. (5) Items 2 (edits.py/shell.py/approve.py/mcp manager.py funnel checks) and 3 (orchestrator spawn/settle_worktree refusal, _PLAN_MODE_ALLOWED = {"ask","researcher","debugger","reviewer"} at agents/orchestrator.py:827) are correctly implemented in isolation and get_diagnostics is clean on the files that own the new logic (edits.py, approve.py, orchestrator.py); base.py's 2 errors and session.py/agent_loop.py/shell.py/mcp manager.py's many errors are all on lines outside this diff's hunks (ProtocolMessage attribute-access and unrelated typing mismatches) and look pre-existing, not newly introduced — not independently confirmed against a clean baseline due to turn budget.

class Subagent(AgentLoop):
    """Same loop as the orch, no user-facing chat stream, no spawn tools."""

    def __init__(self, profile: AgentProfile, **kwargs):
        kwargs.setdefault("role", "subagent")
        kwargs.setdefault("profile", profile.name)
        base = kwargs.pop("system_prompt", profile.system_prompt)
        kwargs["system_prompt"] = f"{(base or '').rstrip()}\n\n{REPORT_TO_ORCH}"
        kwargs.setdefault("write_globs", profile.write_globs)
        # Orch already runs tools in parallel; children were False only because
        # AgentLoop defaulted that way. gather keeps tool_call order; writers
        # serialize via write_lock.
        kwargs.setdefault("concurrent_tools", True)
        # Freeze system (prompt + memory + skills) on first build so cache
        # prefixes stay identical. remember() during this run is in the tool
        # result, not a rewritten system prompt. Siblings' notes wait for orch.
        kwargs.setdefault("freeze_system", True)
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        self._profile = profile
        if profile.max_turns:
            self._config.max_turns = profile.max_turns

    async def finish(self, status: str) -> AgentResult:
        async def complete(payload):
            return await self._llm_complete(payload)

        try:
            return await compress_for_parent(
                self._build_messages(),
                complete=complete,
                status=status,
                required_tools=self._profile.required_tools,
                files_touched=list(self._files_touched),
                tools_called=set(self._tools_called),
            )
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            return AgentResult(
                status=status,
                summary="",
                outcome=f"compaction error: {exc}",
                files_touched=list(self._files_touched),
            )

 8|class Subagent(AgentLoop):
 9|    """Same loop as the orch, no user-facing chat stream, no spawn tools."""
10|
11|    def __init__(self, profile: AgentProfile, **kwargs):
12|        kwargs.setdefault("role", "subagent")
13|        kwargs.setdefault("profile", profile.name)
14|        base = kwargs.pop("system_prompt", profile.system_prompt)
15|        kwargs["system_prompt"] = f"{(base or '').rstrip()}\n\n{REPORT_TO_ORCH}"
16|        kwargs.setdefault("write_globs", profile.write_globs)
17|        # Orch already runs tools in parallel; children were False only because
18|        # AgentLoop defaulted that way. gather keeps tool_call order; writers
19|        # serialize via write_lock.
20|        kwargs.setdefault("concurrent_tools", True)
21|        # Freeze system (prompt + memory + skills) on first build so cache
22|        # prefixes stay identical. remember() during this run is in the tool
23|        # result, not a rewritten system prompt. Siblings' notes wait for orch.
24|        kwargs.setdefault("freeze_system", True)
25|        super().__init__(**kwargs)
26|        self._profile = profile
27|        if profile.max_turns:
28|            self._config.max_turns = profile.max_turns
29|
30|    async def finish(self, status: str) -> AgentResult:
31|        async def complete(payload):
32|            return await self._llm_complete(payload)
33|
34|        try:
35|            return await compress_for_parent(
36|                self._build_messages(),
37|                complete=complete,
38|                status=status,
39|                required_tools=self._profile.required_tools,
40|                files_touched=list(self._files_touched),
41|                tools_called=set(self._tools_called),
42|            )
43|        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
44|            return AgentResult(
45|                status=status,
46|                summary="",
47|                outcome=f"compaction error: {exc}",
48|                files_touched=list(self._files_touched),
49|            )

 33|ORCH_SYSTEM = """You are the orchestrator for this workspace. You talk to the user. You do not implement changes, run tests, investigate bugs, or survey the codebase yourself.
 34|
 35|Spawn a personality by calling it as a tool (ask, coder, tester, researcher, debugger, reviewer). Pass a specific task string: paths, expected outcome, constraints.
 36|
 37|Who does the reading:
 38|- You have no filesystem tools. You cannot list_files, search, or read_file. `ask` is the only reader — after workspace memory has been checked (below).
 39|- `coder` still read_file's a path before editing it (the write funnel requires that). That is not discovery. Your job is to put the paths and facts from memory or ask into the coder task so coder does not have to search or find(1).
 40|
 41|Spawn is fire-and-forget. The tool returns immediately with agent_id (and worktree/branch when the child writes). Do not wait for the child in this turn. Spawn several personalities in one turn only when the work is independent — coder on a feature and debugger on a customer escalation can run at the same time. Tell the user you started them. Do not claim the work is done until a child report arrives.
 42|
 43|Dependent work is sequenced across turns, not inside one turn:
 44|- Need understanding then an edit? If workspace memory already has fresh paths and facts, spawn coder with those. Otherwise spawn ask now. When its report arrives as a follow-up, spawn coder with that report copied in: files, what to change, constraints. Never spawn coder in the same turn you would have needed ask's answer.
 45|- After a code change, spawn tester and/or reviewer the same way — on the previous child's report, not by guessing.
 46|
 47|Writers (coder, tester) run in a git worktree on a new branch under .engine/worktrees/. They will not collide with each other or with the user's checkout. Reviewer joins that worktree so it sees the writer's diff. The user is asked to merge, open a PR, keep, or discard after the writer and any reviewer on that tree have finished. A follow-up engine report says what they chose. Ask, researcher, and debugger use the main workspace.
 48|
 49|When a reviewer requests changes (or a writer's own report leaves something unfinished), the fix belongs in that SAME worktree, not a new one: a fresh coder spawn always branches off the original base commit and is sandboxed to its own new worktree, so it cannot see or reach the prior writer's diff no matter what the task text says. Pass `continue_from=<agent_id>` (the writer's agent_id, e.g. from describe_worktrees or its "started agent_id=..." reply) when spawning coder to have it continue in that exact worktree instead of starting fresh. Only ever have one live coder per worktree at a time.
 50|
 51|Never spawn coder or tester to merge, push, check out the user's branch, or open a pull request. Writers cannot leave their worktree and cannot check out a branch already in use. When the user wants those changes applied — including after a keep — call settle_worktree with merge, pr, or discard. Use action=status if you need the agent_id or branch.
 52|
 53|Check workspace memory before spawning ask:
 54|- Fresh file notes or decision bullets that answer the question: reply from them. Quote the note. Do not spawn.
 55|- STALE file notes, a missing path, or a question the notes do not cover: spawn ask. Put the stale or missing paths in the task. Do not quote a STALE note as fact.
 56|- Deep "explain this subsystem" still spawns ask, but the task must start from the fresh notes (paths, purpose, entry points) rather than rediscovering them.
 57|
 58|For edits, spawn coder. For verification, spawn tester. For a library, API, GitHub repo, error message, or anything not in this workspace, spawn researcher. For "what's broken", spawn debugger. After a code change, spawn reviewer if a verdict is useful.
 59|
 60|A coder/tester task must include: conc

docs/adding-a-command.md  lines 1-200 of 249  (next offset=201)
  1|# Adding a new command
  2|
  3|Commands are the client → server half of the engine's Unix-socket protocol
  4|(NDJSON over `.engine/engine.sock`); events are the server → client half. This
  5|doc covers adding a **command**. If you also need a new outbound message, see
  6|the analogous `@event` pattern in `protocol/events.py` (same idea, registered
  7|in `EVENTS` instead of `COMMANDS`).
  8|
  9|Like tools, commands are declared once and picked up by decorator-based
 10|registries — no central dispatch `if/elif` chain to extend.
 11|
 12|## The pieces
 13|
 14|- `protocol/message.py` — `ProtocolMessage`, the base dataclass every command
 15|  and event inherits. Gives you `to_json()`/`from_json()` for free based on
 16|  dataclass fields and type hints (including `Optional[X]` and `list[X]` of
 17|  another `ProtocolMessage`).
 18|- `protocol/commands.py` — one `@command @dataclass` class per command. The
 19|  `@command` decorator registers the class in `COMMANDS: dict[str, type]` by
 20|  class name, which `decode_command` uses to route an incoming `{"type": ...}`
 21|  JSON object back to the right dataclass.
 22|- `protocol/codec.py` — `encode`/`decode_command`/`decode_event`. NDJSON: one
 23|  JSON object per line, always with a `"type"` field.
 24|- `runtime/commands/register.py` — `HANDLERS: dict[type, callable]` and the
 25|  `@handles(CommandType)` decorator that fills it.
 26|- `runtime/commands/*.py` — handler implementations, grouped by area
 27|  (`lifecycle.py`, `files.py`, `git.py`, `agent.py`). Add a new function to an
 28|  existing module if your command fits, or add a new module.
 29|- `runtime/commands/__init__.py` — imports every handler module for its side
 30|  effects (so the `@handles` decorators run and populate `HANDLERS`). **You
 31|  must add your new module here if you create one** — this is the one place
 32|  that isn't fully automatic (unlike `tools/`, which walks the package
 33|  directory itself).
 34|- `runtime/session.py` — `EngineSession.handle(command)` looks up
 35|  `HANDLERS[type(command)]` and calls it (awaiting if async). This is also
 36|  where most of the state your handler will touch lives (`_state`, `_workspace`,
 37|  `_emit`, `_persist`, ...).
 38|
 39|## Minimal example
 40|
 41|```python
 42|# protocol/commands.py
 43|@command
 44|@dataclass
 45|class RenameSession(ProtocolMessage):
 46|    name: str
 47|```
 48|
 49|```python
 50|# runtime/commands/lifecycle.py (or a new module)
 51|from protocol.commands import RenameSession
 52|from protocol.events import ErrorOccurred
 53|from runtime.commands.register import handles
 54|
 55|
 56|@handles(RenameSession)
 57|def rename_session(session, command: RenameSession) -> None:
 58|    if not session._require_session():
 59|        return
 60|    if not command.name.strip():
 61|        session._emit(ErrorOccurred(message="name must not be empty"))
 62|        return
 63|    session._state.name = command.name.strip()
 64|    session._persist()
 65|```
 66|
 67|If it's a new module, add it to `runtime/commands/__init__.py`:
 68|
 69|```python
 70|from runtime.commands import lifecycle as _lifecycle  # noqa: F401
 71|from runtime.commands import my_module as _my_module  # noqa: F401  # add this
 72|```
 73|
 74|That's the whole integration — the codec already knows how to decode
 75|`RenameSession` (dataclass fields + `@command`), and `EngineSession.handle`
 76|already knows how to route it to `rename_session` (via `HANDLERS`).
 77|
 78|## Defining the command dataclass
 79|
 80|- Inherit `ProtocolMessage`, decorate with `@command` **then** `@dataclass`
 81|  (order matters: `@command` reads `cls.__name__` after the dataclass is
 82|  built, so `@dataclass` must be the inner decorator, applied first).
 83|- Field types matter — `from_json`/`to_json` use them:
 84|  - Plain `str`/`int`/`float`/`bool`/`list[str]` round-trip as-is.
 85|  - `X | None` fields are om

209|    if name in ("context", "orchcontext", "requestorchcontext"):

211|    if name in ("abort", "abortagent"):

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from protocol.commands import SetPlanMode
+from protocol.events import PlanModeChanged
+from runtime.commands.register import handles
+
+
+@handles(SetPlanMode)
+def set_plan_mode(session, command: SetPlanMode) -> None:
+    if not session._require_session():
+        return

class Subagent(AgentLoop):
    """Same loop as the orch, no user-facing chat stream, no spawn tools."""

    def __init__(self, profile: AgentProfile, **kwargs):
        kwargs.setdefault("role", "subagent")
        kwargs.setdefault("profile", profile.name)
        base = kwargs.pop("system_prompt", profile.system_prompt)
        kwargs["system_prompt"] = f"{(base or '').rstrip()}\n\n{REPORT_TO_ORCH}"
        kwargs.setdefault("write_globs", profile.write_globs)
        # Orch already runs tools in parallel; children were False only because
        # AgentLoop defaulted that way. gather keeps tool_call order; writers
        # serialize via write_lock.
        kwargs.setdefault("concurrent_tools", True)
        # Freeze system (prompt + memory + skills) on first build so cache
        # prefixes stay identical. remember() during this run is in the tool
        # result, not a rewritten system prompt. Siblings' notes wait for orch.
        kwargs.setdefault("freeze_system", True)
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        self._profile = profile
        if profile.max_turns:
            self._config.max_turns = profile.max_turns

    async def finish(self, status: str) -> AgentResult:
        async def complete(payload):
            return await self._llm_complete(payload)

        try:
            return await compress_for_parent(
                self._build_messages(),
                complete=complete,
                status=status,
                required_tools=self._profile.required_tools,
                files_touched=list(self._files_touched),
                tools_called=set(self._tools_called),
            )
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            return AgentResult(
                status=status,
                summary="",
                outcome=f"compaction error: {exc}",
                files_touched=list(self._files_touched),
            )

 When a reviewer requests changes (or a writer's own report leaves something unfinished), the fix belongs in that SAME worktree, not a new one: a fresh coder spawn always branches off the original base commit and is sandboxed to its own new worktree, so it cannot see or reach the prior writer's diff no matter what the task text says. Pass `continue_from=<agent_id>` (the writer's agent_id, e.g. from describe_worktrees or its "started agent_id=..." reply) when spawning coder to have it continue in that exact worktree instead of starting fresh. Only ever have one live coder per worktree at a time.
 
 Never spawn coder or tester to merge, push, check out the user's branch, or open a pull request. Writers cannot leave their worktree and cannot check out a branch already in use. When the user wants those changes applied — including after a keep — call settle_worktree with merge, pr, or discard. Use action=status if you need the agent_id or branch.

+Plan mode: when plan mode is active, spawning coder or tester is refused, and settle_worktree is refused (except action=status/list). Investigate using only the read-only personalities — ask, researcher, debugger, reviewer — never coder or tester. Do not spawn coder or tester, and do not call settle_worktree to merge/pr/discard, while plan mode is on — those calls will just error. To proceed, ask the user to approve exiting plan mode using PromptBroker.ask(..., kind="confirm"); only after the user approves, dispatch SetPlanMode(enabled=False) to turn plan mode off, then spawn coder/tester or call settle_worktree normally. If the user does not approve, keep investigating read-only and do not spawn a writer.

I've started a survey agent to map out the codebase — how personalities/tool permissions are structured, where the orchestrator's spawn/tool logic lives, and any existing approval-gating patterns — so I can plan out how to add a "plan mode" (read/explore + propose plan, then user-approved execution, like Claude Code). warn ask 83e28040 $0.515 · 930,455 tok

## Report: Orchestrator/harness architecture for adding "plan mode"

Language/framework: Python 3.9+, asyncio. No web framework — a headless daemon (runtime/server.py) speaking NDJSON-over-Unix-socket (protocol/) to clients (client_tui.py, headless_client.py, dummy_client.py). LLM calls go through llm/openrouter.py (OpenRouter API), abstracted by llm/provider.py.

### 1. Repo structure (top-level)
- agents/ — orchestrator + subagent loop + personality profiles (agents/profiles/*.py)
- runtime/ — session/server plumbing, config, tool implementations' business logic (runtime/tools/*.py), commands (runtime/commands/*.py), mcp, skills, store (sqlite/memory)
- tools/ — thin LLM-facing tool wrappers using @tool decorator (tools/base.py), auto-discovered by tools/registry.py
- protocol/ — dataclass message types for commands/events (protocol/commands.py, protocol/events.py)
- llm/ — OpenRouter client
- docs/ — docs/adding-a-profile.md and docs/adding-a-tool.md are the authoritative "how to extend" guides; docs/impl-plans/orch-subagent-model.md explains the whole spawn/worktree/profile design
- tests/ — pytest suite, incl. tests/test_profiles.py, tests/test_orchestrator.py
- Entry points: app.py, runtime/server.py, runtime/session.py (binds everything: discover_tools(), discover_profiles(), builds Orchestrator)

### 2. Personality/system-prompt definitions Each personality is a module agents/profiles/<name>.py exporting a module-level PROFILE = AgentProfile(...):
- agents/profiles/ask.py — read-only Q&A, write_globs=[], no SHELL/EDIT tools
- agents/profiles/coder.py — full edit + shell, write_globs=None (unrestricted), needs_worktree=True, required_tools=["get_diagnostics"]
- agents/profiles/tester.py — edit+shell but write_globs=TEST_GLOBS (test files only), needs_worktree=True, required_tools=["run_command"]
- agents/profiles/reviewer.py — read-only, write_globs=[], join_worktree=True (joins a writer's worktree to see its diff)
- agents/profiles/debugger.py — has SHELL/GIT/HTTP/browser tools for repro but write_globs=[] (no edits)
- agents/profiles/researcher.py — web/GitHub-repo/docs tools, write_globs=[], no LSP/shell

agents/profile.py defines the AgentProfile dataclass: ``python @dataclassclass AgentProfile: name: str description: str system_prompt: str tool_names: list[str] write_globs: list[str] | None = None # None=any path, []=no writes, list=glob allowlist required_tools: list[str] = field(default_factory=list) max_turns: int = 32 model: str | None = None temperature: float = 0.2 needs_worktree: bool = False join_worktree: bool = False ` and shared tool-name bundles: NAV, SITTER, LSP, EDIT, GIT, SHELL, WEB, BROWSER, GH_READ/GH_WRITE, SKILLS, MEMORY, MCP, etc. discover_profiles() (bottom of file) walks agents/profiles/ via pkgutil and registers every PROFILE, so there is no central registry file to edit to add a personality — dropping a new module is enough. ProfileRegistry.as_tools(spawn_fn) turns each profile into a callable tool (_spawn_tool) exposed to the orchestrator model.

The orchestrator's own system prompt (ORCH_SYSTEM, top of agents/orchestrator.py) explains spawn semantics, sequencing rules, and explicitly says "Do not call write tools or run_command. You do not have them" — the orchestrator itself has zero filesystem/write tools; only SKILLS + MEMORY plus one spawn-tool per profile plus settle_worktree.

### 3. Tool/function definitions (spawn, activate_skill, remember, settle_worktree)
- spawn-as-tool: not a fixed tool — generated per profile in agents/profile.py:_spawn_tool(), wired in agents/orchestrator.py:__init__ via for spec in profiles.as_tools(self.spawn): self._tools.register(spec). Real implementation is Orchestrator.spawn(profile_name, task, continue_from="") (agents/orchestrator.py:455), which creates a Subagent (agents/subagent.py) in a background asyncio.Task, optionally in a git worktree.
- settle_worktree: built by _settle_worktree_tool(orch) (agents/orchestrator.py:825), registered alongside spawn tools; calls Orchestrator.apply_named_worktree → runtime/tools/git.apply_worktree (merge/pr/keep/discard). This is the closest existing analog to a "user approval gate before landing a change" — see #5 below.
- activate_skill / read_skill: tools/skills.py, thin wrappers calling runtime/skills/discover.py / SkillCatalog (runtime/skills/catalog.py).
- remember: tools/remember.py → runtime/store/memory.py:remember(), persists to .engine/memory.json.
- All generic tools use the @tool decorator pattern in tools/base.py (Tool dataclass with .schema()/.execute(), tool() decorator attaches _engine_tool attr) and are auto-discovered by tools/registry.py:discover_tools() (walks tools/ package, no manual registry edit, same "drop a file" pattern as profiles).

### 4. Mode/permission gating — how it currently works There is no "mode" concept today, only static per-profile permissions fixed at profile-definition time:
1. tool_names (allowlist) — controls which tool *names* a spawned child's ToolRegistry.subset() even exposes to the model (tools/registry.py:subset). A personality without EDIT/SHELL in its bundle literally cannot call those tools.
2. write_globs — enforced deeper in the write funnel regardless of which edit tool is called. runtime/tools/edits.py:_profile_write_error(ctx, path) reads ctx.write_globs (set from AgentProfile.write_globs onto ToolContext in agents/agent_loop.py/agents/subagent.py) and calls runtime/tools/writeglob.py:write_allowed(rel, globs). None=unrestricted, []=hard no-write, list=fnmatch allowlist. This runs inside apply_edit(), the single choke-point all edit tools funnel through (str_replace, replace_lines, create_file, apply_patch, replace_symbol, etc., all in tools/edit_file.py/tools/apply_patch.py/tools/edit_symbol.py, all calling into runtime/tools/edits.py).
3. required_tools — soft signal only (marks AgentResult.status="incomplete" if unused by finish), not an enforcement mechanism.

docs/adding-a-profile.md explicitly documents this: *"The allowlist and write_globs are enforced. Do not rely on the system prompt alone to keep a personality read-only."*

To add a "plan mode" you have two design options given this architecture:
- Option A (cheapest, matches existing pattern exactly): add a new personality agents/profiles/plan.py with write_globs=[] and no EDIT/SHELL tool names (just NAV+SITTER+LSP+SKILLS+MEMORY, maybe GIT read tools) — this gives you an ask/reviewer-style read-only planning profile today, callable as plan(task=...). This is the "propose a plan" half but does not give a stateful mode switch inside one running agent.
- Option B (true mode-switch within one agent's run): needs a new runtime concept, since currently permissions are fixed for the whole life of a spawned Subagent/AgentLoop instance (write_globs and tool_names are baked in at _make_subagent/spawn time, agents/orchestrator.py:744 _make_subagent, and never mutated mid-run). You would need to:
- Add a plan_mode: bool (or similar) field to ToolContext (tools/base.py) and/or AgentLoop/Subagent state, defaulting True for a "planning" personality.
- Gate _profile_write_error in runtime/tools/edits.py (and run_command in tools/shell.py) on that flag in addition to write_globs.
- Add a way to flip it off: either a new tool (e.g. exit_plan_mode/approve_plan) that the model calls, gated by require_approval-style ctx.ask_user(question, kind="confirm") (pattern already in runtime/tools/approve.py), or a protocol Command (like protocol/commands.py:AnswerPrompt) that the user sends after reviewing a plan text the agent produced.
- Orchestrator-level equivalent: since orchestrator itself has no write tools and always delegates to coder/tester via spawn(), a simpler system-level plan-mode could instead gate Orchestrator.spawn() (agents/orchestrator.py:455) itself — block spawning coder/tester (or any profile with needs_worktree/non-empty write_globs) until the user has confirmed a pending plan, then allow it. This would only require changes in agents/orchestrator.py (spawn()) plus a new state flag and a new approval command/tool, not touching every profile file.

### 5. Existing user-approval/confirmation gating Yes, already present and directly reusable as a template:
- runtime/tools/approve.py:require_approval(ctx, question) — generic confirm gate keyed on ctx.config.exec_approval (auto|always|never, env ENGINE_EXEC_APPROVAL, runtime/config.py). Used by tools/github.py (PR/issue create & comment) and tools/http.py (mutating HTTP verbs). Calls ctx.ask_user(question, kind="confirm").
- tools/shell.py:run_command does its own equivalent inline (approve() closure) before running mutating commands, also reading exec_approval.
- agents/orchestrator.py:_settle_worktree — after a writer (coder/tester) finishes and has a dirty worktree, it always prompts the user via self._child_ask_user(question, kind="choice", choices=SETTLE_CHOICES, default="keep") asking merge/pr/keep/discard before anything lands on the user's checkout branch. This is the closest existing analogue to "propose, then get approval before executing" — plan mode's "approve to proceed" step should likely reuse PromptBroker.ask() (runtime/prompts.py) the same way, either via kind="confirm" or kind="choice".
- The prompt plumbing itself: runtime/prompts.py:PromptBroker emits protocol/events.py:UserPromptRequested, and the client answers via protocol/commands.py:AnswerPrompt(prompt_id, text), handled in runtime/session.py. This is the transport-level mechanism any new "approve this plan" UX would ride on.

### 6. Agent loop / spawn mechanics
- agents/agent_loop.py:AgentLoop — the core model-call + tool-dispatch loop (shared by orchestrator and subagents): builds messages, calls LLM (llm/openrouter.py), dispatches tool calls via ToolRegistry.execute, handles compaction (agents/compactor.py), turn budgets, skills catalog rendering, memory rendering.
- agents/subagent.py:Subagent(AgentLoop) — child agent variant: freezes system prompt (freeze_system=True) for prompt-cache stability, appends REPORT_TO_ORCH boilerplate, no spawn tools, finish(status) compacts transcript into an AgentResult (agents/compactor.py) that becomes the orchestrator's follow-up message (children never talk to the user directly).
- agents/orchestrator.py:Orchestrator(AgentLoop) — adds spawn/worktree/settle machinery on top of the same loop. spawn() creates a Subagent via _make_subagent() (builds ToolContext-bearing child with tools=self._all_tools.subset(profile.tool_names, profile=profile.name), write_lock, isolated LSP if in a worktree) and runs it as a fire-and-forget asyncio.Task; result flows back as an inbox message tagged [agent ... finished] handled by runtime/session.py.
- Wiring: runtime/session.py calls discover_tools() + discover_profiles() and constructs the Orchestrator, passing callbacks for prompts (self._prompts.ask as child_ask_user), events, etc.

### Leftover
- Could not find any existing "plan"/"dry-run"/"propose" personality or partial implementation in the codebase — this is a genuinely new feature, not an existing toggle to flip.
- No existing mid-run mode-switch mechanism on AgentProfile/ToolContext/AgentLoop — confirmed by reading agents/agent_loop.py construction and agents/orchestrator.py:_make_subagent; permissions are fixed at spawn time from the static AgentProfile. Building true "plan then execute after approval in the same conversation" requires the option-B design above; a coder should confirm which UX is wanted (separate plan personality vs. stateful mode flag on coder`) before implementing.

  1|# Adding a subagent profile
  2|
  3|Profiles are discovered the same way tools are: drop a module under
  4|`agents/profiles/`, export `PROFILE = AgentProfile(...)`, and the orchestrator
  5|picks it up on the next `StartSession`. There is no registry file to edit.
  6|
  7|The orchestrator sees each profile as a **tool named after the profile**. Calling
  8|`ask` / `coder` / `tester` / … starts that child and returns immediately with
  9|`agent_id` (and `worktree` / `branch` when the profile writes). The child runs in
 10|the background. Tokens stream to the client tagged with `agent_id`. When it finishes, its transcript is compacted into an
 11|`AgentResult` string and delivered to the orch as a follow-up message (not as
 12|the original tool result). The child never chats with the user.
 13|
 14|## Who reads vs who writes
 15|
 16|The orchestrator is the planner, not a third reader. Typical edit:
 17|
 18|1. Spawn **ask** with the survey question. Stop. Do not also spawn coder in that turn.
 19|2. When ask's report arrives, spawn **coder** with paths, facts, and the change copied into the task.
 20|3. Coder `read_file`s those named paths (required before an edit) and writes. It should not `find` / search the tree unless a named path is missing.
 21|
 22|Skip a separate planner personality — that is the orch. Independent work (coder on a feature and debugger on an escalation) still runs in the same turn.
 23|
 24|## Minimal example
 25|
 26|```python
 27|# agents/profiles/docs.py
 28|from agents.profile import NAV, AgentProfile
 29|
 30|PROFILE = AgentProfile(
 31|    name="docs",
 32|    description="Write or update markdown docs. Cannot edit application code.",
 33|    system_prompt="You only touch documentation files. ...",
 34|    tool_names=NAV + ["str_replace", "create_file", "read_file"],
 35|    write_globs=["**/*.md", "**/docs/**"],
 36|    required_tools=[],
 37|    max_turns=8,
 38|    needs_worktree=False,
 39|)
 40|```
 41|
 42|Restart the session (or call `discover_profiles()` in a test). The orch model
 43|will see a `docs` tool with a `task` argument.
 44|
 45|## Examples
 46|
 47|Three end-to-end recipes, from simplest to most involved.
 48|
 49|### Example A: a profile with no tools at all
 50|
 51|Some personalities only need to reason over the task text and conversation
 52|history — no filesystem, no shell, nothing. Set `tool_names=[]` and
 53|`write_globs=[]` so it is a hard no-op even if a future edit to the profile
 54|accidentally adds a tool name.
 55|
 56|```python
 57|# agents/profiles/planner.py
 58|from __future__ import annotations
 59|from agents.profile import AgentProfile
 60|
 61|PLANNER_SYSTEM = """You are a planning-only agent. You do not read files,
 62|run commands, or edit anything. Given a task description and any facts
 63|already provided in the prompt, produce a short ordered plan (steps, owners,
 64|risks). If you need information you were not given, say so explicitly and
 65|stop — do not guess at file paths or code contents."""
 66|
 67|PROFILE = AgentProfile(
 68|    name="planner",
 69|    description=(
 70|        "Turns a fuzzy task into an ordered plan using only the text it was "
 71|        "given. Has no tools — cannot read the repo or verify anything. Use "
 72|        "only when the caller already has the facts and just wants them "
 73|        "organized."
 74|    ),
 75|    system_prompt=PLANNER_SYSTEM,
 76|    tool_names=[],
 77|    write_globs=[],
 78|    required_tools=[],
 79|    max_turns=4,
 80|    needs_worktree=False,
 81|)
 82|```
 83|
 84|Nothing else to wire up — dropping this file under `agents/profiles/` is the
 85|entire registration step. Restart the session (or call `discover_profiles()`
 86|in a test) and the orch model will see a `planner(task=...)` tool.
 87|
 88|### Example B: a profile reusing existing tools
 89|
 90|Most new personalities just need a different combination of to

11|    def __init__(self, profile: AgentProfile, **kwargs):
12|        kwargs.setdefault("role", "subagent")
13|        kwargs.setdefault("profile", profile.name)
14|        base = kwargs.pop("system_prompt", profile.system_prompt)

16|        kwargs.setdefault("write_globs", profile.write_globs)
17|        # Orch already runs tools in parallel; children were False only because
18|        # AgentLoop defaulted that way. gather keeps tool_call order; writers
19|        # serialize via write_lock.
20|        kwargs.setdefault("concurrent_tools", True)
21|        # Freeze system (prompt + memory + skills) on first build so cache
22|        # prefixes stay identical. remember() during this run is in the tool
23|        # result, not a rewritten system prompt. Siblings' notes wait for orch.
24|        kwargs.setdefault("freeze_system", True)
25|        super().__init__(**kwargs)

40|                files_touched=list(self._files_touched),
