203|  `runtime/session.py`'s `_bind_loop()`, so restarting the session (or
204|   calling both functions directly in a test) picks up the new tool and the
205|   new profile at the same time — there is nothing to wire by hand in either
206|   direction.
207|2. Add tests: a `discover_tools()` assertion that `todo_scanner` is present
208|  with no registry errors (see the pattern in `tests/test_tools_registry.py`),
209|   and — if `auditor` should be a permanent builtin personality — add
210|   `"auditor"` to the name set asserted in
211|   `tests/test_profiles.py::test_discover_builtin_profiles`.
212|
213|
214|
215|## `AgentProfile` fields
216|
217|- `name` — tool name the orch calls. Must be unique.
218|- `description` — shown to the orch so it can choose. Be specific about what
219|this personality will not do.
220|- `system_prompt` — the child's only system prompt (plus workspace memory rendered from
221|`.engine/memory.json`). Subagents freeze that system text on the first model call so
222|prompt-cache prefixes stay stable; `remember()` during the child's own run is visible
223|as a tool result, not as a rewritten system block. The orchestrator re-renders every turn.
224|Ask, coder, and researcher briefings are ingested into the main workspace
225|`memory.json` when the child finishes (hashed in the child's tree, including
226|worktrees). Mid-run `remember` can still write a better structured note; ingest
227|will not overwrite a **fresh** file note. STALE notes (disk hash ≠ `note_sha`)
228|are rewritten from the briefing.
229|- `tool_names` — allowlist from `discover_tools()`. Unknown names become
230|registry errors, not a crash. Never include other personality names. Include
231|`MEMORY` (`remember`) unless the personality truly has nothing to persist.
232|- `write_globs` — `None` means any workspace path the write funnel already
233|allows; `[]` means no writes even if an edit tool was wired by mistake; a
234|list is matched against the relative path (`**/tests/**`, `**/*.md`, …).
235|- `required_tools` — if these names never appear in the child's tool trace,
236|`AgentResult.status` is `incomplete` (the child still exits). Used by `coder`
237|(`get_diagnostics`) and `tester` (`run_command`).
238|- `max_turns` — child's own cap, independent of the orch. Built-in profiles use 32. Hitting it prompts continue (same child, another `turn_slice`), handoff (orch may spawn one writer with leftover), or stop (no respawn). `ENGINE_TURN_CONTINUE=never` skips the prompt and hands off. Do not lower researcher without `Stats.agent_runs` showing frequent `max_turns`; spawn-once still blocks a sibling researcher, so a hard cut just wastes the survey.
239|- `model` — optional OpenRouter model id for this personality. `tester` uses Haiku; ask/researcher/coder/debugger/reviewer inherit `OPENROUTER_MODEL`. `OPENROUTER_CHILD_MODEL` overrides only profiles that leave `model` unset.
240|- `needs_worktree` — if true, the child runs in a git worktree on a new branch
241|under `.engine/worktrees/` so writers do not collide. `coder` and `tester`
242|set this. When the child finishes with changes, those edits are committed on
243|the writer branch, then the user is prompted to merge, open a PR, keep, or
244|discard — after any `join_worktree` personality (reviewer) on that tree has
245|also finished. Later "please merge it" goes through `settle_worktree`, not a
246|new writer spawn.
247|- `join_worktree` — if true, the child reuses a live writer worktree (same
248|batch if possible) instead of creating one. `reviewer` sets this so it sees
249|the writer's diff. If no worktree is open, it uses the main checkout.
250|
251|
252|
253|## Hard vs prompt-only
254|
255|The allowlist and `write_globs` are enforced. Do not rely on the system prompt
256|alone to keep a personality read-only. `requi

   1|# Engine
   2|
   3|![coverage](coverage.svg)
   4|
   5|A headless backend for an AI coding agent.
   6|
   7|Engine runs as a long-lived process bound to one workspace. It exposes a
   8|newline-delimited JSON protocol over a Unix domain socket, so any client — a
   9|TUI, a web app, an editor plugin, a test harness — can drive an LLM coding
  10|agent without importing a single line of agent internals. The orchestrator
  11|spawns named personalities (ask, coder, tester, …) that share tools for
  12|reading, searching, understanding, and editing code, backed by
  13|tree-sitter for instant syntax queries and the Language Server Protocol for
  14|real type information.
  15|
  16|The design goal is a hard boundary. Clients speak JSON; they never touch the
  17|orchestrator, the tool registry, or the LLM client. Everything crossing the
  18|socket is a dataclass with a `type` field.
  19|
  20|---
  21|
  22|## Table of contents
  23|
  24|- [Why this exists](#why-this-exists)
  25|- [Quick start](#quick-start)
  26|- [Architecture](#architecture)
  27|- [The protocol](#the-protocol)
  28|  - [Commands](#commands-client--engine)
  29|  - [Events](#events-engine--client)
  30|  - [Snapshots and reconnection](#snapshots-and-reconnection)
  31|- [The agent loop](#the-agent-loop)
  32|- [Tools](#tools)
  33|  - [Discovery and reload](#discovery-and-reload)
  34|  - [The full tool catalogue](#the-full-tool-catalogue)
  35|  - [Writing a new tool](#writing-a-new-tool)
  36|- [The write funnel](#the-write-funnel)
  37|  - [Read-before-edit](#read-before-edit)
  38|  - [The write guard](#the-write-guard)
  39|  - [File identity preservation](#file-identity-preservation)
  40|  - [The syntax gate](#the-syntax-gate)
  41|  - [Atomic writes and the edit journal](#atomic-writes-and-the-edit-journal)
  42|  - [Undo](#undo)
  43|- [Language support](#language-support)
  44|  - [Detection](#detection)
  45|  - [Tree-sitter](#tree-sitter)
  46|  - [Language servers](#language-servers)
  47|- [Persistence](#persistence)
  48|- [Configuration](#configuration)
  49|- [The reference client](#the-reference-client)
  50|- [Testing](#testing)
  51|- [Project layout](#project-layout)
  52|- [Operational limits](#operational-limits)
  53|- [Extending the engine](#extending-the-engine)
  54|- [Implementation plans](#implementation-plans)
  55|- [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)
  56|
  57|---
  58|
  59|## Why this exists
  60|
  61|Most agent frameworks fuse the model loop, the tool implementations, and the
  62|user interface into one process. That makes the interesting part — the tool
  63|layer that actually touches your code — hard to test and impossible to reuse.
  64|
  65|Engine separates them:
  66|
  67|- **The core** (`EngineSession`) owns the workspace, the agent loop, the tool
  68|  registry, and session state.
  69|- **The contract** (`protocol/`) is a set of JSON dataclasses. Commands come
  70|  in, events go out. Nothing else crosses the line.
  71|- **The transport** (`EngineServer`) is NDJSON over a Unix socket today. The
  72|  same message types would work over a WebSocket or HTTP without touching the
  73|  core.
  74|
  75|The practical payoff is that the write path can be paranoid. Because editing
  76|is funnelled through one module rather than scattered across tool
  77|implementations, every write gets staleness checks, a symlink and denylist
  78|guard, newline and encoding preservation, a tree-sitter syntax gate, an atomic
  79|replace, and a journal entry that makes it undoable. A tool author writes a
  80|pure `str -> str` function and inherits all of it.
  81|
  82|---
  83|
  84|## Quick start
  85|
  86|### Requirements
  87|
  88|| Requirement | Notes |
  89||---|---|
  90|| Python 3.9+ | The protocol layer has an explicit fallback for 3.9's lack of runtime PEP 604 unions |
  91|| An OpenRouter API key | Required for the agent loop; the engine boots without on

 39|- `coder` still read_file's a path before editing it (the write funnel requires that). That is not discovery. Your job is to put the paths and facts from memory or ask into the coder task so coder does not have to search or find(1).
 40|

Spawn several personalities in one turn only when the work is independent — coder on a feature and debugger on a customer escalation can run at the same time. Tell the user you started them. Do not claim the work is done until a child report arrives.
 42|
 43|Dependent work is sequenced across turns, not inside one turn:
 44|- Need understanding then an edit? If workspace memory already has fresh paths and facts, spawn coder with those. Otherwise spawn ask now. When its report arrives as a follow-up, spawn coder with that report copied in: files, what to change, constraints. Never spawn coder in the same turn you would have needed ask's answer.
 45|- After a code change, spawn tester and/or reviewer the same way — on the previous child's report, not by guessing.
 46|
 47|Writers (coder, tester) run in a git worktree on a new branch under .engine/worktrees/. They will not collide with each other or with the user's checkout. Reviewer joins that worktree so it sees the writer's diff. The user is asked to merge, open a PR, keep, or discard after the writer and any reviewer on that tree have finished. A follow-up engine report says what they chose. Ask, researcher, and debugger use the main workspace.
 48|
 49|When a reviewer requests changes (or a writer's own report leaves something unfinished), the fix belongs in that SAME worktree, not a new one: a fresh coder spawn always branches off the original base commit and is sandboxed to its own new worktree, so it cannot see or reach the prior writer's diff no matter what the task text says. Pass `continue_from=<agent_id>` (the writer's agent_id, e.g. from describe_worktrees or its "started agent_id=..." reply) when spawning coder to have it continue in that exact worktree instead of starting fresh. +def _enter_plan_mode_tool(orch: Orchestrator) -> Tool:
+    async def execute(ctx: ToolContext) -> str:  # noqa: ARG001
+        orch.plan_mode = True
+        return (
+            "plan mode is now on. Explore with read-only agents only "
+            "(ask, researcher, debugger, reviewer) -- do not spawn coder or "
+            "tester while in this mode. When you have a concrete plan, call "
+            "present_plan with it so the user can approve or reject it."
+        )
+
+    return Tool(
+        name="enter_plan_mode",
+        description=(
+            "Switch into read-only plan mode: explore with ask/researcher/"
+            "debugger/reviewer, then call present_plan for user approval "
+            "before any coder/tester spawn is allowed."
+        ),
+        parameters={"type": "object", "properties": {}},
+        fn=execute,
+    )
+
+
+def _present_plan_tool(orch: Orchestrator) -> Tool:
+    async def execute(ctx: ToolContext, plan: str) -> str:  # noqa: ARG001
+        if not orch.plan_mode:
+            return "error: not in plan mode; call enter_plan_mode first"
+        question = (
+            "Proposed plan:\n\n"
+            f"{plan}\n\n"
+            "Approve this plan? Approving allows coder/tester spawns."
+        )
+        answer = "no"
+        if orch._child_ask_user is not None:
+            answer = await orch._child_ask_user(question, kind="confirm")
+        if str(answer).strip().lower() in {"yes", "y"}:
+            orch.plan_mode = False
+            return "plan approved; plan mode is now off. coder/tester spawns are allowed."
+        return (
+            "plan rejected; still in plan mode. User feedback: "
+            f"{answer}. Revise the plan and call present_plan again."
+        )
+
+    return Tool(
+        name="present_plan",
+        description=(
+            "Present a proposed plan to the user for approval while in plan "
+            "mode. Must be called before spawning coder/tester. If rejected, "
+            "revise and call again."
+        ),
+        parameters={
+            "type": "object",
+            "properties": {

+                    "description": "The proposed plan text, shown to the user verbatim.",
+                },
+            },
+            "required": ["plan"],
+        },
+        fn=execute,

Explore with those read-only agents, then call present_plan(plan) with a concrete plan (files, changes, order of operations) so the user can approve or reject it. If approved, plan mode turns off and you may spawn coder/tester. If rejected, the user's feedback comes back as the tool result — revise the plan and call present_plan again.
 
 Do not call write tools or run_command. You do not have them.

        action: str,
        agent_id: str = "",
        branch: str = "",

                "branch": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "description": "Optional branch name (or substring) if agent_id is unknown.",
                },
            },
            "required": ["action"],
        },
        fn=execute,
    )

async def spawn(self, profile_name: str, task: str, continue_from: str = "") -> str:
        try:
            profile = self._profiles.get(profile_name)
        except KeyError:
            return f"error: unknown profile {profile_name}"
        if self.plan_mode and profile.needs_worktree:
            return (
                f"error: plan mode is active; call present_plan and get user "
                f"approval before spawning {profile_name}"
            )
        if self._spawn_lock is None:
            self._spawn_lock = asyncio.Lock()
        async with self._spawn_lock:
            # First user turn (_inbox_turn False) may fan out ask+researcher
            # in parallel. Only leftover inbox turns after "[agent … finished]"
            # are blocked from respawning the same survey profile.
            if (
                profile_name in _SURVEY_ONCE
                and profile_name in self._user_survey_spawns
                and self._inbox_turn
            ):
                if profile_name not in self._survey_retry:
                    return (
                        f"error: already spawned {profile_name} this user message; "
                        "answer with what you have or ask the user"
                    )
                self._survey_retry.discard(profile_name)
                self._survey_retry_used.add(profile_name)
            if self._live_spawn_count() >= self._spawn_budget:
                return "error: spawn budget exhausted"
            agent_id = uuid4().hex
            self._reserved.add(agent_id)
            if profile_name in _SURVEY_ONCE:
                self._user_survey_spawns.add(profile_name)
            batch_id = self._batch_id or uuid4().hex
            batch_name = self._batch_name or batch_nickname(task)
        worktree = ""
        branch = ""
        warning = ""
        child_workspace = self._ctx.workspace
        try:
            if continue_from:
                if not profile.needs_worktree:
                    raise RuntimeError(
                        f"continue_from is only for writers (coder, tester); "
                        f"{profile.name} does not use its own worktree"
                    )
                dest = self._worktrees.get(continue_from)
                if dest is None or not dest.is_dir():
                    raise RuntimeError(
                        f"no open worktree for agent_id={continue_from!r} "
                        "(already settled, discarded, or never spawned) -- "
                        "call describe_worktrees to see what's still open"
                    )
                worktree = str(dest)
                branch = self._worktree_branches.get(continue_from, "")
                child_workspace = dest
                owner_batch = self._worktree_batches.get(continue_from, batch_id)
                # Transfer ownership to the new agent_id rather than also
                # remembering it under continue_from -- the agent being
                # continued from is already finished, and leaving both
                # agent_ids pointing at the same directory would settle
                # (push/PR/merge) it twice.
                self._forget_worktree(continue_from)
                self._remember_worktree(
                    agent_id, dest, branch, profile.name, owner_batch
                )
                warning = f" (continuing {continue_from[:8]}'s worktree)"
            elif profile.needs_worktree:
                path, branch, err = await asyncio.to_thread(
                    add_agent_worktree,
                    self._ctx.workspace,
                    agent_id,
                    profile.name,
                )
                if err:
                    warning = f" (worktree unavailable: {err}; using main workspace)"
                    branch = ""
                else:
                    worktree = path

Author:     Iresh Sharma <32684272+iresharma@users.noreply.github.com>

    Fix test suite after merging batch coverage PRs (#30)
    
    * engine(tester): what / Completed three new test files from scratch raising coverage on t
    
    * engine(tester): what / Created three new test files with 186 tests total to improve cove
    
    * Fix test suite after merging the batch of coverage PRs
    
    The 14 auto-generated "engine(tester)" coverage PRs merged into main
    introduced tests that didn't match this codebase's conventions or the
    real API surface, plus one genuine production bug:
    
    - Add pytest-asyncio and asyncio_mode=auto: the new tests used bare
      `async def test_*` with @pytest.mark.asyncio, which this repo never
      supported (existing convention wraps async code in asyncio.run()).
    - Fix runtime/tools/sitter.py: modern tree-sitter (>=0.22) moved
      Query.captures() onto QueryCursor; query_tree was broken for real,
      not just in tests.
    - Rewrite hallucinated test assumptions (nonexistent kwargs/attributes
      on AgentLoop/Orchestrator, wrong dataclass fields, wrong patch
      targets, wrong exception message assertions) to match actual code.
    - Fix tests/test_shell.py: a raw `asyncio.create_subprocess_shell =`
      monkeypatch was never restored, poisoning every later test that
      shells out for real; switched to the monkeypatch fixture.
    - Ignore __pycache__/ and *.py[cod] in .gitignore.
    
    Full suite: 1166 passed, 0 failed.

12|
13|class ToolRegistry:
14|    def __init__(self) -> None:
15|        self._tools: dict[str, Tool] = {}
16|        self.errors: list[str] = []
17|
18|    def register(self, spec: Tool) -> None:
19|        if spec.name in self._tools:
20|            self.errors.append(f"duplicate tool name: {spec.name}")
21|            return
22|        self._tools[spec.name] = spec
23|
24|    def names(self) -> set[str]:
25|        return set(self._tools)
26|
27|    def subset(self, names: list[str], profile: str = "") -> ToolRegistry:
28|        out = ToolRegistry()
29|        seen: set[str] = set()
30|        for name in names:
31|            if name == "mcp":
32|                for spec in self._tools.values():
33|                    if spec.family != "mcp" or spec.name in seen:
34|                        continue
35|                    if not _mcp_allowed(spec, profile):
36|                        continue
37|                    seen.add(spec.name)
38|                    out._tools[spec.name] = spec
39|                continue
40|            if name in seen:
41|                continue
42|            seen.add(name)
43|            spec = self._tools.get(name)
44|            if spec is None:
45|                out.errors.append(f"unknown tool: {name}")
46|                continue
47|            out._tools[name] = spec
48|        return out
49|
50|    def drop_family(self, family: str) -> None:
51|        self._tools = {
52|            name: spec for name, spec in self._tools.items() if spec.family != family
53|        }
54|
55|    def schemas(self) -> list[dict]:
56|        return [spec.schema() for spec in self._tools.values()]
57|
58|    async def execute(self, name: str, ctx: ToolContext, arguments: dict) -> str:
59|        spec = self._tools.get(name)
60|        if spec is None:
61|            return f"error: unknown tool {name}"
62|        try:
63|            text = await spec.execute(ctx, arguments)
64|        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
65|            return f"error: {exc}"
66|        if len(text) > MAX_RESULT:
67|            return text[:MAX_RESULT] + "\n...[truncated]"
68|        return text
69|
70|
71|def discover_tools() -> ToolRegistry:
72|    """Import every module under tools/ except this file and base.py."""
73|    registry = ToolRegistry()
74|    prefix = tools_pkg.__name__ + "."
75|    skip = {tools_pkg.__name__ + ".base", tools_pkg.__name__ + ".registry"}
76|    for info in pkgutil.walk_packages(tools_pkg.__path__, prefix):
77|        if info.name in skip or info.name.rsplit(".", 1)[-1].startswith("_"):
78|            continue
79|        try:
80|            module = importlib.import_module(info.name)
81|            module = importlib.reload(module)
82|        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
83|            registry.errors.append(f"{info.name}: {exc}")
84|            continue
85|        for value in vars(module).values():
86|            spec = getattr(value, "_engine_tool", None)
87|            if isinstance(spec, Tool):
88|                registry.register(spec)
89|    return registry

 35|Spawn a personality by calling it as a tool (ask, coder, tester, researcher, debugger, reviewer). Pass a specific task string: paths, expected outcome, constraints.

 37|Who does the reading:

 39|- `coder` still read_file's a path before editing it (the write funnel requires that). That is not discovery. Your job is to put the paths and facts from memory or ask into the coder task so coder does not have to search or find(1).
 40|
 41|Spawn is fire-and-forget. The tool returns immediately with agent_id (and worktree/branch when the child writes). Do not wait for the child in this turn. Spawn several personalities in one turn only when the work is independent — coder on a feature and debugger on a customer escalation can run at the same time. Tell the user you started them.  42|
 43|Dependent work is sequenced across turns, not inside one turn:
 44|- Need understanding then an edit? If workspace memory already has fresh paths and facts, spawn coder with those. Otherwise spawn ask now. When its report arrives as a follow-up, spawn coder with that report copied in: files, what to change, constraints. Never spawn coder in the same turn you would have needed ask's answer.
 45|- After a code change, spawn tester and/or reviewer the same way — on the previous child's report, not by guessing.
 46|
 47|Writers (coder, tester) run in a git worktree on a new branch under .engine/worktrees/. They will not collide with each other or with the user's checkout. Reviewer joins that worktree so it sees the writer's diff. The user is asked to merge, open a PR, keep, or discard after the writer and any reviewer on that tree have finished. A follow-up engine report says what they chose. Ask, researcher, and debugger use the main workspace.

Pass `continue_from=<agent_id>` (the writer's agent_id, e.g. from describe_worktrees or its "started agent_id=..." reply) when spawning coder to have it continue in that exact worktree instead of starting fresh.  33|ORCH_SYSTEM = """You are the orchestrator for this workspace. You talk to the user. You do not implement changes, run tests, investigate bugs, or survey the codebase yourself.
 34|
 35|Spawn a personality by calling it as a tool (ask, coder, tester, researcher, debugger, reviewer). Pass a specific task string: paths, expected outcome, constraints.
 36|
 37|Who does the reading:
 38|- You have no filesystem tools. You cannot list_files, search, or read_file. `ask` is the only reader — after workspace memory has been checked (below).
 39|- `coder` still read_file's a path before editing it (the write funnel requires that). That is not discovery. Your job is to put the paths and facts from memory or ask into the coder task so coder does not have to search or find(1).
 40|
 41|Spawn is fire-and-forget. The tool returns immediately with agent_id (and worktree/branch when the child writes). Do not wait for the child in this turn. Spawn several personalities in one turn only when the work is independent — coder on a feature and debugger on a customer escalation can run at the same time. Tell the user you started them. Do not claim the work is done until a child report arrives.
 42|
 43|Dependent work is sequenced across turns, not inside one turn:
 44|- Need understanding then an edit? If workspace memory already has fresh paths and facts, spawn coder with those. Otherwise spawn ask now. When its report arrives as a follow-up, spawn coder with that report copied in: files, what to change, constraints. Never spawn coder in the same turn you would have needed ask's answer.
 45|- After a code change, spawn tester and/or reviewer the same way — on the previous child's report, not by guessing.
 46|
 47|Writers (coder, tester) run in a git worktree on a new branch under .engine/worktrees/. They will not collide with each other or with the user's checkout. Reviewer joins that worktree so it sees the writer's diff. The user is asked to merge, open a PR, keep, or discard after the writer and any reviewer on that tree have finished. A follow-up engine report says what they chose. Ask, researcher, and debugger use the main workspace.
 48|
 49|When a reviewer requests changes (or a writer's own report leaves something unfinished), the fix belongs in that SAME worktree, not a new one: a fresh coder spawn always branches off the original base commit and is sandboxed to its own new worktree, so it cannot see or reach the prior writer's diff no matter what the task text says. Pass `continue_from=<agent_id>` (the writer's agent_id, e.g. from describe_worktrees or its "started agent_id=..." reply) when spawning coder to have it continue in that exact worktree instead of starting fresh. Everything checks out. Final status on plan mode:

Implementation (agents/orchestrator.py, branch engine/coder/59528518fc274cabb541971d80505050):
- Orchestrator.plan_mode: bool = False
- enter_plan_mode() tool — switches into read-only planning, guides the model to only use ask/researcher/debugger/reviewer
- present_plan(plan) tool — presents the plan to you via the same confirm-prompt channel _settle_worktree already uses (kind="confirm"); "yes"/"y" (case-insensitive) turns plan mode off and unblocks writer spawns; anything else keeps it on and returns your feedback to the model to revise
- spawn() gated generically on profile.needs_worktree (currently coder/tester) — checked before any side effect (no worktree/subagent/task created if blocked), so ask/researcher/debugger/reviewer are unaffected
- Orchestrator system prompt updated to document the flow

Verification:
- Reviewer: approved the logic point-for-point — correct gate ordering, no hardcoded profile names, consistent approval-string convention, coherent prompt wording, no unrelated files touched.
- Tester: added 17 new tests for plan-mode behavior (init, block/unblock, approve/reject, case-insensitivity, gate-before-side-effect, unaffected read-only profiles). Full suite now 62/62 passing (39 in test_orchestrator_coverage.py + 23 in test_orchestrator.py).

The only thing the reviewer flagged (tester touching tests/test_orchestrator_coverage.py) was expected — that's the tester's own added coverage, not a violation of the coder's "don't touch tests" instruction (that instruction applied to the coder, not the tester).
